guide:closed-tropical-rect.tip: This sealed container recycles its own water — it transpires, condenses on the glass, and runs back to the substrate, so a balanced one needs water only rarely, often just every few months. Read the glass rather than watering on a timer: light fog that clears by midday is healthy; if the walls go bone-dry, add a light mist; if they stay fogged solid for 48 hours or more, vent it for a few hours first before adding anything.

This sealed container naturally traps ambient moisture to maintain high humidity levels (70%-85%). Monitor for excessive glass condensation; if the walls remain completely fogged for over 48 hours, open the enclosure for a few hours to vent stale air, then reseal.
Place in a medium indirect light environment or a few feet back from a primary light window. Avoid deep, dark corners as well as intense, burning direct sun rays.

Mixed growth rates detected within the enclosure (moderate, slow). Regular pruning intervals are highly recommended: monitor fast-growing elements closely and trim them back regularly to prevent them from choking out slower companions or creating canopy shadows that block valuable light.

Place in a location that receives several hours of direct sunlight daily. Monitor temperature closely, as enclosed glass containers can create a greenhouse effect and overheat rapidly under direct sun rays.
